content.content:
1	---
2	title: Release 1.18
3	description: 'cert-manager release notes: cert-manager 1.18'
4	---
5	
6	cert-manager is the easiest way to automatically manage certificates in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.
7	
8	cert-manager 1.18 introduces several new features and breaking changes.
9	Highlights include support for ACME certificate profiles,
10	a new default for `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` now set to `Always` (breaking change), and
11	the default `Certificate.Spec.RevisionHistoryLimit` now set to `1` (potentially breaking).
12	Be sure to review all new features and changes below, and read the full release notes carefully before upgrading.
13	
14	## Major Themes
15	
16	### OperatorHub Packages Discontinued
17	
18	We no longer publish OperatorHub packages for cert-manager.
19	Why? Because the cert-manager maintainers no longer have the time or resources to maintain and test those packages.
20	cert-manager `v1.16.5` is the last release on OperatorHub.
21	
22	> ℹ️ [cert-manager `v1.16.5` for RedHat OpenShift OperatorHub](https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod/tree/main/operators/cert-manager/1.16.5).
23	>
24	> ℹ️ [cert-manager `v1.16.5` for `operatorhub.io`](https://github.com/k8s-operatorhub/community-operators/tree/main/operators/cert-manager/1.16.5).
25	>
26	> ℹ️ [Archived `cert-manager-olm` repository](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager-olm).
27	
28	### ACME HTTP01 challenge paths now use `PathType` `Exact` in Ingress routes
29	
30	> ⚠️ Breaking change
31	
32	We have changed the `PathType` for ACME HTTP01 Ingress-based challenges to `Exact`.
33	This security feature ensures that the challenge path (which is an exact path)
34	is not misinterpreted as a regular expression or some other Ingress-specific
35	(`ImplementationSpecific`) parsing.
36	This allows HTTP01 challenges to be solved when using standards compliant
37	Ingress controllers such as Cilium.
38	
39	This change is incompatible with certain versions and configurations of the `ingress-nginx` Ingress controller.
40	Versions of [`ingress-nginx >=1.8.0`](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/main/changelog/controller-1.8.0.md) support a [`strict-validate-path-type` configuration option](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/user-guide/nginx-configuration/configmap/#strict-validate-path-type) which, when enabled, disallows `.` (dot) in the path value. This is a [bug](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/issues/11176) which makes it impossible to use various legitimate URL paths, including the  `http://<YOUR_DOMAIN>/.well-known/acme-challenge/<TOKEN>` URLs used for [ACME HTTP01](https://letsencrypt.org/docs/challenge-types/#http-01-challenge).
41	To make matters worse, the buggy validation is [enabled by default](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/pull/11819) in [`ingress-nginx >= 1.12.0`](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/main/changelog/controller-1.12.0.md).
42	You will see errors like this in the cert-manager controller logs:
43	
44	> Error presenting challenge: admission webhook `validate.nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io` denied the request: ingress contains invalid paths: path `/.well-known/acme-challenge/oTw4h9_WsobTRn5COTSyaiAx3aWn0M7_aYisoz1gXQw` cannot be used with `pathType` Exact
45	
46	If you use `ingress-nginx`, choose **one** of the following three options:
47	
48	#### Option 1. Disable the `ACMEHTTP01IngressPathTypeExact` feature in cert-manager
49	
50	To disable the `ACMEHTTP01IngressPathTypeExact` feature,
51	to reinstate the old `PathType: ImplementationSpecific` behavior,
52	use the following Helm values when installing cert-manager:
53	
54	```yaml
55	# values.yaml
56	config:
57	  featureGates:
58	    # Disable the use of Exact PathType in Ingress resources, to work around a bug in ingress-nginx
59	    # https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/issues/11176
60	    ACMEHTTP01IngressPathTypeExact: false
61	```
62	
63	#### Option 2. Disable the `strict-validate-path-type` option in ingress-nginx
64	
65	To disable the buggy strict path validation,
66	use the following Helm values when installing `ingress-nginx`:
67	
68	```yaml
69	# values.yaml
70	controller:
71	  config:
72	    # Disable strict path validation, to work around a bug in ingress-nginx
73	    # https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/issues/11176
74	    strict-validate-path-type: false
75	```
76	
77	#### Option 3. Upgrade `ingress-nginx`
78	
79	This issue is resolved in `ingress-nginx` versions `v1.13.2` and `v1.12.6`, both released on August 29, 2025.
80	
81	If you are running ingress-nginx `v1.13.2+` or `v1.12.6+`, you do not need to apply the workarounds described above.
82	
83	See the [fix commit](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/commit/618aae18515213bcf3fb820e6f8c234703d844b2)
84	
85	#### OpenShift's built-in Ingress-to-Route conversion
86	
87	This change is also incompatible with OpenShift's built-in router, which is unrelated to the ingress-nginx options above.
88	OpenShift's Ingress-to-Route conversion skips rules which use `pathType: Exact`, so the HTTP01 challenge fails with a 503 response.
89	See [OpenShift](../../installation/compatibility.md#openshift) on the compatibility page for details and the feature gate to disable.
90	
91	### ACME Certificate Profiles
92	
93	cert-manager now supports the selection of ACME certificate profiles, allowing
94	users to request different categories of certificates from their ACME
95	Certificate Authority.
96	This enhancement leverages the latest [ACME protocol extension for certificate profiles (IETF draft)][rfc] and is supported by Let's Encrypt and other providers.
97	For example, Let's Encrypt offers the [`tlsserver`][tlsserver] profile for
98	standard server certificates and the [`shortlived`][shortlived] profile for
99	short-lived six-day certificates.
100	These new options provide users with greater flexibility and improved security
101	for their certificate management needs.
102	
103	[rfc]: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-aaron-acme-profiles/
104	[tlsserver]: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/profiles/#tlsserver
105	[shortlived]: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/profiles/#shortlived
106	
107	> 📖 Learn more by visiting the [ACME Issuer documentation](../../configuration/acme/README.md#acme-certificate-profiles).
108	
109	### The default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` is now `Always`
110	
111	> ⚠️ Breaking change
112	
113	We have changed the default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` from `Never` to `Always`.
114	
115	Why? Because the old default was unintuitive and insecure.
116	For example, if a private key is exposed, users may (reasonably) assume that
117	re-issuing a certificate (e.g. using `cmctl renew`) will generate a new private
118	key, but it won't unless the user has explicitly set `rotationPolicy: Always` on the Certificate resource.
119	
120	This change is feature gated and is enabled by default, because it has been fast-tracked to beta status.
121	
122	Users who want to preserve the old default have two options:
123	1. Explicitly set `rotationPolicy: Never` on your Certificate resources.
124	2. Turn off the feature gate in this release and explicitly set
125	   `rotationPolicy: Never` on your Certificates before release 1.19.
126	   In release 1.19, the feature will be marked as GA and it will no longer be
127	   possible to turn off the feature.
128	
129	The following Helm chart values can be used to turn off the feature gate:
130	
131	```yaml
132	# values.yaml
133	config:
134	  featureGates:
135	    DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false
136	```
137	
138	> ℹ️ The old default value `Never` was always intended to be changed before API `v1`, as can be seen in the description of the [original PR](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/2814):
139	> > For backward compatibility, the empty value is treated as 'Never' which matches the behavior we have today.
140	> > In a future API version, we can flip this default to be Always.
141	>
142	> 📖 See [Issue: 7601: Change `PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` to default to Always](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/7601) to read the proposal for this change and the discussion around it.
143	>
144	> 📖 Read [cert-manager component configuration](../../installation/configuring-components.md) to learn more about feature gates.
145	>
146	> 📖 Read our updated [API compatibility statement](../../contributing/api-compatibility.md) which now reflects our new, more flexible, approach to changing API defaults, with a view to introducing other "sane" default API values in future releases.
147	>
148	> 📖 Read [Issuance behavior: Rotation of the private key](../../usage/certificate.md#issuance-behavior-rotation-of-the-private-key) to learn more about private key rotation in cert-manager.
149	
150	
151	### The default value of `Certificate.Spec.RevisionHistoryLimit` is now `1`
152	
153	> ⚠️ Potentially breaking change
154	
155	The default value for the `Certificate` resource's `revisionHistoryLimit` field is now set to 1.
156	This ensures that old `CertificateRequest` revisions are automatically garbage collected, improving resource management and reducing clutter in clusters.
157	Previously, if not specified, no limit was applied, potentially leading to an accumulation of stale `CertificateRequest` resources.
158	With this update, users no longer need to manually configure the revision history limit to benefit from automated cleanup.
159	
160	When you upgrade to cert-manager 1.18, all stale `CertificateRequest` resources will be garbage collected, unless you explicitly set the `revisionHistoryLimit` value on your `Certificate` resources.
161	
162	### Copy annotations from Ingress or Gateway to the Certificate
163	
164	We've added a new configuration option to the cert-manager controller: `--extra-certificate-annotations`, which allows you to specify annotation keys to be copied from an Ingress or Gateway resource to the resulting Certificate object.
165	Read [Annotated Ingress resource: Copy annotations to the Certificate](../../usage/ingress.md#copy-annotations-to-the-certificate ), and
166	[Annotated Gateway resource: Copy annotations to the Certificate](../../usage/gateway.md#copy-annotations-to-the-certificate), to learn more.
167	
168	## Community
169	
170	As always, we'd like to thank all of the community members who helped in this release cycle, including all below who merged a PR and anyone that helped by commenting on issues, testing, or getting involved in cert-manager meetings. We're lucky to have you involved.

---
title: Release 1.18
description: 'cert-manager release notes: cert-manager 1.18'
---

cert-manager is the easiest way to automatically manage certificates in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

cert-manager 1.18 introduces several new features and breaking changes.
Highlights include support for ACME certificate profiles,
a new default for `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` now set to `Always` (breaking change), and
the default `Certificate.Spec.RevisionHistoryLimit` now set to `1` (potentially breaking).
Be sure to review all new features and changes below, and read the full release notes carefully before upgrading.

## Major Themes

### OperatorHub Packages Discontinued

We no longer publish OperatorHub packages for cert-manager.
Why? Because the cert-manager maintainers no longer have the time or resources to maintain and test those packages.
cert-manager `v1.16.5` is the last release on OperatorHub.

> ℹ️ [cert-manager `v1.16.5` for RedHat OpenShift OperatorHub](https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod/tree/main/operators/cert-manager/1.16.5).
>
> ℹ️ [cert-manager `v1.16.5` for `operatorhub.io`](https://github.com/k8s-operatorhub/community-operators/tree/main/operators/cert-manager/1.16.5).
>
> ℹ️ [Archived `cert-manager-olm` repository](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager-olm).

### ACME HTTP01 challenge paths now use `PathType` `Exact` in Ingress routes

> ⚠️ Breaking change

We have changed the `PathType` for ACME HTTP01 Ingress-based challenges to `Exact`.
This security feature ensures that the challenge path (which is an exact path)
is not misinterpreted as a regular expression or some other Ingress-specific
(`ImplementationSpecific`) parsing.
This allows HTTP01 challenges to be solved when using standards compliant
Ingress controllers such as Cilium.

This change is incompatible with certain versions and configurations of the `ingress-nginx` Ingress controller.
Versions of [`ingress-nginx >=1.8.0`](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/main/changelog/controller-1.8.0.md) support a [`strict-validate-path-type` configuration option](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/user-guide/nginx-configuration/configmap/#strict-validate-path-type) which, when enabled, disallows `.` (dot) in the path value. This is a [bug](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/issues/11176) which makes it impossible to use various legitimate URL paths, including the  `http://<YOUR_DOMAIN>/.well-known/acme-challenge/<TOKEN>` URLs used for [ACME HTTP01](https://letsencrypt.org/docs/challenge-types/#http-01-challenge).
To make matters worse, the buggy validation is [enabled by default](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/pull/11819) in [`ingress-nginx >= 1.12.0`](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/main/changelog/controller-1.12.0.md).
You will see errors like this in the cert-manager controller logs:

> Error presenting challenge: admission webhook `validate.nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io` denied the request: ingress contains invalid paths: path `/.well-known/acme-challenge/oTw4h9_WsobTRn5COTSyaiAx3aWn0M7_aYisoz1gXQw` cannot be used with `pathType` Exact

If you use `ingress-nginx`, choose **one** of the following three options:

#### Option 1. Disable the `ACMEHTTP01IngressPathTypeExact` feature in cert-manager

To disable the `ACMEHTTP01IngressPathTypeExact` feature,
to reinstate the old `PathType: ImplementationSpecific` behavior,
use the following Helm values when installing cert-manager:

```yaml
# values.yaml
config:
  featureGates:
    # Disable the use of Exact PathType in Ingress resources, to work around a bug in ingress-nginx
    # https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/issues/11176
    ACMEHTTP01IngressPathTypeExact: false
```

#### Option 2. Disable the `strict-validate-path-type` option in ingress-nginx

To disable the buggy strict path validation,
use the following Helm values when installing `ingress-nginx`:

```yaml
# values.yaml
controller:
  config:
    # Disable strict path validation, to work around a bug in ingress-nginx
    # https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/issues/11176
    strict-validate-path-type: false
```

#### Option 3. Upgrade `ingress-nginx`

This issue is resolved in `ingress-nginx` versions `v1.13.2` and `v1.12.6`, both released on August 29, 2025.

If you are running ingress-nginx `v1.13.2+` or `v1.12.6+`, you do not need to apply the workarounds described above.

See the [fix commit](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/commit/618aae18515213bcf3fb820e6f8c234703d844b2)

#### OpenShift's built-in Ingress-to-Route conversion

This change is also incompatible with OpenShift's built-in router, which is unrelated to the ingress-nginx options above.
OpenShift's Ingress-to-Route conversion skips rules which use `pathType: Exact`, so the HTTP01 challenge fails with a 503 response.
See [OpenShift](../../installation/compatibility.md#openshift) on the compatibility page for details and the feature gate to disable.

### ACME Certificate Profiles

cert-manager now supports the selection of ACME certificate profiles, allowing
users to request different categories of certificates from their ACME
Certificate Authority.
This enhancement leverages the latest [ACME protocol extension for certificate profiles (IETF draft)][rfc] and is supported by Let's Encrypt and other providers.
For example, Let's Encrypt offers the [`tlsserver`][tlsserver] profile for
standard server certificates and the [`shortlived`][shortlived] profile for
short-lived six-day certificates.
These new options provide users with greater flexibility and improved security
for their certificate management needs.

[rfc]: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-aaron-acme-profiles/
[tlsserver]: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/profiles/#tlsserver
[shortlived]: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/profiles/#shortlived

> 📖 Learn more by visiting the [ACME Issuer documentation](../../configuration/acme/README.md#acme-certificate-profiles).

### The default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` is now `Always`

> ⚠️ Breaking change

We have changed the default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` from `Never` to `Always`.

Why? Because the old default was unintuitive and insecure.
For example, if a private key is exposed, users may (reasonably) assume that
re-issuing a certificate (e.g. using `cmctl renew`) will generate a new private
key, but it won't unless the user has explicitly set `rotationPolicy: Always` on the Certificate resource.

This change is feature gated and is enabled by default, because it has been fast-tracked to beta status.

Users who want to preserve the old default have two options:
1. Explicitly set `rotationPolicy: Never` on your Certificate resources.
2. Turn off the feature gate in this release and explicitly set
   `rotationPolicy: Never` on your Certificates before release 1.19.
   In release 1.19, the feature will be marked as GA and it will no longer be
   possible to turn off the feature.

The following Helm chart values can be used to turn off the feature gate:

```yaml
# values.yaml
config:
  featureGates:
    DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false
```

> ℹ️ The old default value `Never` was always intended to be changed before API `v1`, as can be seen in the description of the [original PR](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/2814):
> > For backward compatibility, the empty value is treated as 'Never' which matches the behavior we have today.
> > In a future API version, we can flip this default to be Always.
>
> 📖 See [Issue: 7601: Change `PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` to default to Always](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/7601) to read the proposal for this change and the discussion around it.
>
> 📖 Read [cert-manager component configuration](../../installation/configuring-components.md) to learn more about feature gates.
>
> 📖 Read our updated [API compatibility statement](../../contributing/api-compatibility.md) which now reflects our new, more flexible, approach to changing API defaults, with a view to introducing other "sane" default API values in future releases.
>
> 📖 Read [Issuance behavior: Rotation of the private key](../../usage/certificate.md#issuance-behavior-rotation-of-the-private-key) to learn more about private key rotation in cert-manager.


### The default value of `Certificate.Spec.RevisionHistoryLimit` is now `1`

> ⚠️ Potentially breaking change

The default value for the `Certificate` resource's `revisionHistoryLimit` field is now set to 1.
This ensures that old `CertificateRequest` revisions are automatically garbage collected, improving resource management and reducing clutter in clusters.
Previously, if not specified, no limit was applied, potentially leading to an accumulation of stale `CertificateRequest` resources.
With this update, users no longer need to manually configure the revision history limit to benefit from automated cleanup.

When you upgrade to cert-manager 1.18, all stale `CertificateRequest` resources will be garbage collected, unless you explicitly set the `revisionHistoryLimit` value on your `Certificate` resources.

### Copy annotations from Ingress or Gateway to the Certificate

We've added a new configuration option to the cert-manager controller: `--extra-certificate-annotations`, which allows you to specify annotation keys to be copied from an Ingress or Gateway resource to the resulting Certificate object.
Read [Annotated Ingress resource: Copy annotations to the Certificate](../../usage/ingress.md#copy-annotations-to-the-certificate ), and
[Annotated Gateway resource: Copy annotations to the Certificate](../../usage/gateway.md#copy-annotations-to-the-certificate), to learn more.

## Community

As always, we'd like to thank all of the community members who helped in this release cycle, including all below who merged a PR and anyone that helped by commenting on issues, testing, or getting involved in cert-manager meetings. We're lucky to have you involved.

A special thanks to:

- [`@terinjokes`](https://github.com/terinjokes)
- [`@solidDoWant`](https://github.com/solidDoWant)
- [`@k0da`](https://github.com/k0da)
- [`@ali-hamza-noor`](https://github.com/ali-hamza-noor)
- [`@tareksha`](https://github.com/tareksha)
- [`@ThatsIvan`](https://github.com/ThatsIvan)
- [`@jsoref`](https://github.com/jsoref)
- [`@jcpunk`](https://github.com/jcpunk)
- [`@teslaedison`](https://github.com/teslaedison)
- [`@NicholasBlaskey`](https://github.com/NicholasBlaskey)
- [`@sspreitzer`](https://github.com/sspreitzer)
- [`@tsaarni`](https://github.com/tsaarni)

## `v1.18.6`

A simple bug-fix release to address [`CVE-2025-68121`](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h355-32pf-p2xm). All users should upgrade.

Note that no efforts were made to patch [`CVE-2026-24051`](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9h8m-3fm2-qjrq) - this vulnerability only affects macOS and as such does not affect cert-manager running in Kubernetes clusters.

### Changes by Kind

#### Bug or Regression

- Bump Go to address `CVE-2025-68121` ([#8525](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8525), [@SgtCoDFish](https://github.com/SgtCoDFish))

## `v1.18.5`

This release contains three bug fixes, including a fix for the moderate severity DoS issue in [`GHSA-gx3x-vq4p-mhhv`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/security/advisories/GHSA-gx3x-vq4p-mhhv).

All users should upgrade to the latest release. Thanks to Oleh Konko for reporting the issue!

### Changes by Kind

#### Bug or Regression

- Fixed an infinite re-issuance loop that could occur when an issuer returns a certificate with a public key that doesn't match the CSR. The issuing controller now validates the certificate before storing it and fails with backoff on mismatch. ([#8414](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8414), [@cert-manager-bot](https://github.com/cert-manager-bot))
- Fixed an issue where HTTP-01 challenges failed when the Host header contains an IPv6 address. This means that users can now issue IP address certificates for IPv6 address subjects. ([#8437](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8437), [@cert-manager-bot](https://github.com/cert-manager-bot))
- Security (MODERATE): Fix a potential panic in the cert-manager controller when a DNS response in an unexpected order was cached. If an attacker was able to modify DNS responses (or if they controlled the DNS server) it was possible to cause denial of service for the cert-manager controller. ([#8467](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8467), [@SgtCoDFish](https://github.com/SgtCoDFish))

#### Other (Cleanup or Flake)

- Bump go to 1.24.12 ([#8460](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8460), [@SgtCoDFish](https://github.com/SgtCoDFish))

## `v1.18.4`

We updated Go to fix some vulnerabilities in the Go standard library.

Changes since `v1.18.3`:

### Bug or Regression

- Address false positive vulnerabilities `CVE-2025-47914` and `CVE-2025-58181` which were reported by Trivy. ([`#8282`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8282), [`@SgtCoDFish`](https://github.com/SgtCoDFish))
- Update Go to `v1.24.11` to fix `CVE-2025-61727` and `CVE-2025-61729` ([`#8295`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8295), [`@wallrj-cyberark`](https://github.com/wallrj-cyberark))

### Other (Cleanup or Flake)

- Update cert-manager's ACME client, forked from `golang/x/crypto` ([`#8271`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8271), [`@SgtCoDFish`](https://github.com/SgtCoDFish))
- Updated Debian 12 distroless base images ([`#8328`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8328), [`@wallrj-cyberark`](https://github.com/wallrj-cyberark))

## `v1.18.3`

We fixed a bug which caused certificates to be re-issued unexpectedly, if the
`issuerRef` kind or group was changed to one of the "runtime" default values.
We increased the size limit when parsing PEM certificate chains to handle leaf
certificates with large numbers of DNS named or other identities.
We upgraded Go to `1.24.9` to fix various non-critical security vulnerabilities.

Changes since `v1.18.2`:

### Bug or Regression

- BUGFIX: in case kind or group in the `issuerRef` of a Certificate was omitted, upgrading to `1.19.x` incorrectly caused the certificate to be renewed ([`#8174`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8174), [`@cert-manager-bot`](https://github.com/cert-manager-bot))
- Bump Go to `1.24.9`. Fixes the following vulnerabilities: `CVE-2025-61724`, `CVE-2025-58187`, `CVE-2025-47912`, `CVE-2025-58183`, `CVE-2025-61723`, `CVE-2025-58186`, `CVE-2025-58185`, `CVE-2025-58188`, `CVE-2025-61725` ([`#8176`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/8176), [`@wallrj-cyberark`](https://github.com/wallrj-cyberark))
- Increase maximum sizes of PEM certificates and chains which can be parsed in cert-manager, to handle leaf certificates with large numbers of DNS names or other identities ([`#7966`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7966), [`@cert-manager-bot`](https://github.com/cert-manager-bot))

### Other (Cleanup or Flake)

- Improve error messages when certificates, CRLs or private keys fail admission due to malformed or missing PEM data ([`#7964`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7964), [`@cert-manager-bot`](https://github.com/cert-manager-bot))
- Upgrades Go to `v1.24.6` ([`#7974`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7974), [`@SgtCoDFish`](https://github.com/SgtCoDFish))

## `v1.18.2`

We fixed a bug in the CSR's name constraints construction (only applies if you have enabled the `NameConstraints` feature gate).
We dropped the new `global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole` Helm option due to a bug we found, this feature will be released in `v1.19` instead.

Changes since `v1.18.1`:

### Bug or Regression

- BUGFIX: permitted URI domains were incorrectly used to set the excluded URI domains in the CSR's name constraints ([`#7833`][#7833])
- Reverted adding the `global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole` Helm option. ([`#7837`][#7837])

[#7833]: https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/7833
[#7837]: https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/7837

## `v1.18.1`

We have added a new feature gate `ACMEHTTP01IngressPathTypeExact`, to allow
`ingress-nginx` users to turn off the new default Ingress `PathType: Exact`
behavior, in ACME HTTP01 Ingress challenge solvers.

We have increased the ACME challenge authorization timeout to two minutes, which we hope will fix a timeout error (`error waiting for authorization`), which has been reported by multiple users, since the release of cert-manager `v1.16.0`.
This change should fix the following issues: [`#7337`][#7337], [`#7444`][#7444], and [`#7685`][#7685].

[#7337]: https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/7337
[#7444]: https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/7444
[#7685]: https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/7685

Changes since `v1.18.0`:

### Feature

- Added a new feature gate `ACMEHTTP01IngressPathTypeExact`, to allow `ingress-nginx` users to turn off the new default Ingress `PathType: Exact` behavior, in ACME HTTP01 Ingress challenge solvers. ([`#7810`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7810), [`@sspreitzer`](https://github.com/sspreitzer))

### Bug or Regression

- ACME: Increased challenge authorization timeout to 2 minutes to fix `error waiting for authorization`. ([`#7801`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7801), [`@hjoshi123`](https://github.com/hjoshi123))

### Other (Cleanup or Flake)

- Use the latest version of ingress-nginx in E2E tests to ensure compatibility ([`#7807`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7807), [`@wallrj`](https://github.com/wallrj))

## `v1.18.0`

Changes since `v1.17.2`:

### Feature

- Add config to the Vault issuer to allow the server-name to be specified when validating the certificates the Vault server presents. ([`#7663`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7663), [`@ThatsMrTalbot`](https://github.com/ThatsMrTalbot))
- Added `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: cert-manager` label to the created Let's Encrypt account keys ([`#7577`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7577), [`@terinjokes`](https://github.com/terinjokes))
- Added certificate issuance and expiration time metrics (`certmanager_certificate_not_before_timestamp_seconds`, `certmanager_certificate_not_after_timestamp_seconds`). ([`#7612`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7612), [`@solidDoWant`](https://github.com/solidDoWant))
- Added ingress-shim option `--extra-certificate-annotations`, which sets a list of annotation keys to be copied from Ingress-like to resulting Certificate object ([`#7083`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7083), [`@k0da`](https://github.com/k0da))
- Added the `iss` short name for the cert-manager `Issuer` resource
- Added the `ciss` short name for the cert-manager `ClusterIssuer` resource ([`#7373`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7373), [`@SgtCoDFish`](https://github.com/SgtCoDFish))
- Adds the `global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole` helm value to disable HTTP-01 ACME challenges. This allows cert-manager to drop its permission to create pods, improving security when HTTP-01 challenges are not required. ([`#7666`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7666), [`@ali-hamza-noor`](https://github.com/ali-hamza-noor))
- Allow customizing signature algorithm ([`#7591`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7591), [`@tareksha`](https://github.com/tareksha))
- Cache the full DNS response and handle TTL expiration in `FindZoneByFqdn` ([`#7596`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7596), [`@ThatsIvan`](https://github.com/ThatsIvan))
- Cert-manager now uses a local fork of the `golang.org/x/crypto/acme` package ([`#7752`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7752), [`@wallrj`](https://github.com/wallrj))
- Add support for [`ACME profiles extension`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-aaron-acme-profiles/). ([`#7777`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7777), [`@wallrj`](https://github.com/wallrj))
- Promote the `UseDomainQualifiedFinalizer` feature to GA. ([`#7735`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7735), [`@jsoref`](https://github.com/jsoref))
- Switched `service/servicemon` definitions to use port names instead of numbers. ([`#7727`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7727), [`@jcpunk`](https://github.com/jcpunk))
- The default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` changed from `Never` to `Always`. ([`#7723`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7723), [`@wallrj`](https://github.com/wallrj))
- Set the default `revisionHistoryLimit` to 1 for the CertificateRequest revisions ([`#7758`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7758), [`@ali-hamza-noor`](https://github.com/ali-hamza-noor))

### Documentation

- Fix some comments ([`#7620`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7620), [`@teslaedison`](https://github.com/teslaedison))

### Bug or Regression

- Bump `go-jose` dependency to address `CVE-2025-27144`. ([`#7606`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7606), [`@SgtCoDFish`](https://github.com/SgtCoDFish))
- Bump `golang.org/x/oauth2` to patch `CVE-2025-22868`.
- Bump `golang.org/x/crypto` to patch `GHSA-hcg3-q754-cr77`.
- Bump `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt` to patch `GHSA-mh63-6h87-95cp`. ([`#7638`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7638), [`@NicholasBlaskey`](https://github.com/NicholasBlaskey))
- Change of the Kubernetes Ingress `pathType` from `ImplementationSpecific` to `Exact` for a reliable handling of ingress controllers and enhanced security. ([`#7767`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7767), [`@sspreitzer`](https://github.com/sspreitzer))
- Fix AWS Route53 error detection for not-found errors during deletion of DNS records. ([`#7690`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7690), [`@wallrj`](https://github.com/wallrj))
- Fix behavior when running with `--namespace=<namespace>`: limit the scope of cert-manager to a single namespace and disable cluster-scoped controllers. ([`#7678`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7678), [`@tsaarni`](https://github.com/tsaarni))
- Fix handling of certificates with IP addresses in the `commonName` field; IP addresses are no longer added to the DNS `subjectAlternativeName` list and are instead added to the `ipAddresses` field as expected. ([`#7081`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7081), [`@johnjcool`](https://github.com/johnjcool))
- Fix issuing of certificates via DNS01 challenges on Cloudflare after a breaking change to the Cloudflare API ([`#7549`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7549), [`@LukeCarrier`](https://github.com/LukeCarrier))
- Fixed the `certmanager_certificate_renewal_timestamp_seconds` metric help text indicating that the metric is relative to expiration time, rather than Unix epoch time. ([`#7609`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7609), [`@solidDoWant`](https://github.com/solidDoWant))
- Fixing the service account template to incorporate boolean values for the annotations. ([`#7698`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7698), [`@ali-hamza-noor`](https://github.com/ali-hamza-noor))
- Quote nodeSelector values in Helm Chart ([`#7579`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7579), [`@tobiasbp`](https://github.com/tobiasbp))
- Skip Gateway TLS listeners in `Passthrough` mode. ([`#6986`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/6986), [`@vehagn`](https://github.com/vehagn))
- Upgrade `golang.org/x/net` fixing `CVE-2025-22870`. ([`#7619`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7619), [`@depandabot[bot]`](https://github.com/apps/dependabot))

### Other (Cleanup or Flake)

- ACME E2E Tests: Upgraded Pebble to `v2.7.0` and modified the ACME tests to match latest Pebble behavior. ([`#7771`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7771), [`@wallrj`](https://github.com/wallrj))
- Patch the `third_party/forked/acme` package with support for the ACME profiles extension. ([`#7776`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7776), [`@wallrj`](https://github.com/wallrj))
- Promote the `AdditionalCertificateOutputFormats` feature to GA, making additional formats always enabled. ([`#7744`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7744), [`@erikgb`](https://github.com/erikgb))
- Remove deprecated feature gate `ValidateCAA`. Setting this feature gate is now a no-op which does nothing but print a warning log line ([`#7553`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7553), [`@SgtCoDFish`](https://github.com/SgtCoDFish))
- Upgrade `golang.org/x/net` fixing `CVE-2025-22870`. ([`#7619`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7619), [`@depandabot[bot]`](https://github.com/apps/dependabot))
- Update kind images to include the Kubernetes 1.33 node image ([`#7787`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7787), [`@wallrj`](https://github.com/wallrj))
- Upgrade Go to `v1.24.4` ([`#7785`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7785), [`@wallrj`](https://github.com/wallrj))
- Use `slices.Contains` to simplify code ([`#7753`](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/pull/7753), [`@cuinix`](https://github.com/cuinix))

# checkout calls ledger over mutual TLS: it presents its own certificate and
# verifies ledger against the CA certificate in its own Secret (ca.crt).
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: checkout
  labels:
    app: checkout
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: checkout
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: checkout
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: checkout
          image: curlimages/curl:8.10.1
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              while true; do
                curl -sS --max-time 5 \
                  --cacert /tls/ca.crt --cert /tls/tls.crt --key /tls/tls.key \
                  https://ledger.payments.svc/ || echo "ledger call failed"
                sleep 30
              done
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tls
              mountPath: /tls
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: tls
          secret:
            secretName: checkout-tls

metadata:
  name: cert-manager
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "0"
spec:
  project: platform
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: cert-manager
  sources:
    - repoURL: https://charts.jetstack.io
      chart: cert-manager
      targetRevision: v1.17.2
      helm:
        releaseName: cert-manager
        valueFiles:
          - $values/platform/cert-manager/values.yaml
    - repoURL: https://git.example.com/platform/gitops-payments-us.git
      targetRevision: main
      ref: values
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
    syncOptions:
      - CreateNamespace=true
      - ServerSideApply=true

Summary

535

Challenge resources under acme.cert-manager.io can be created directly by namespace users. On create, cert-manager performs no admission validation tying the Challenge to an Order, an owner reference, or an Issuer-selected solver. The ACME Challenge controller then reconciles the direct resource and uses Challenge.spec.solver as the DNS01 provider configuration.

536

When the direct Challenge references a ClusterIssuer, cert-manager derives the DNS provider secret namespace and ambient-credential policy from the ClusterIssuer reference, but the DNS provider configuration itself is attacker-controlled through Challenge.spec.solver. Description

Summary

Challenge resources under acme.cert-manager.io can be created directly by namespace users. On create, cert-manager performs no admission validation tying the Challenge to an Order, an owner reference, or an Issuer-selected solver. The ACME Challenge controller then reconciles the direct resource and uses Challenge.spec.solver as the DNS01 provider configuration.

When the direct Challenge references a ClusterIssuer, cert-manager derives the DNS provider secret namespace and ambient-credential policy from the ClusterIssuer reference, but the DNS provider configuration itself is attacker-controlled through Challenge.spec.solver. This lets a namespace user bypass Issuer/ClusterIssuer solver selectors such as dnsZones, dnsNames, and matchLabels, and make the cert-manager controller use ClusterIssuer DNS credentials for attacker-selected provider settings and DNS names.

In the acme-dns case, this becomes credential disclosure because the attacker-controlled solver host receives the X-Api-User and X-Api-Key headers loaded by cert-manager from the ClusterIssuer resource namespace.

Attack preconditions

  • The attacker can create challenges.acme.cert-manager.io resources in at least one namespace.
  • The cert-manager controller is running and reconciles ACME Challenge resources cluster-wide.
  • A usable ClusterIssuer exists in the cluster.
  • The referenced ClusterIssuer has a DNS01 solver that uses a Secret in the cluster resource namespace, or relies on ambient credentials enabled for ClusterIssuer.
  • The cluster is multi-tenant or otherwise separates namespace users from platform-owned Issuer/ClusterIssuer and DNS credential administration.

Severity

Rationale: a tenant with namespace-level ACME Challenge create permissions, including permissions granted by cert-manager's aggregate edit role, can cause a cluster-scoped controller to use DNS credentials or ambient cloud credentials outside the Issuer's intended solver policy. With acme-dns specifically, this can disclose the referenced acme-dns account credential to an attacker-controlled endpoint. With other DNS providers, the impact is credential use, Issuer policy bypass, and unauthorized DNS mutation risk unless a provider-specific credential disclosure path is separately demonstrated.

Why this is not just RBAC misconfiguration

cert-manager's documented end-user workflow does not require users to manually create Challenge resources. # cert-manager v1.17.2 -> v1.18.0: impact assessment for the prod payments cluster

## Verdict

**No documented breaking change is a hard blocker for this environment, but the upgrade is not a no-op. One breaking change (the `rotationPolicy` default flip) changes runtime behaviour for two live Certificates, and one (the `revisionHistoryLimit` default) deletes data on first reconcile.**
The upgrade is acceptable to proceed with, subject to the pre-flight checks at the end. The most important check is one I could not perform from this repository: confirming that the rendered `mesh-root-ca` carries `rotationPolicy: Never` and that the live nginx and curl workloads cope with key rotation.

## What this environment actually uses

- cert-manager is installed from the Helm chart with minimal values (`env/platform/cert-manager/values.yaml`): CRDs enabled and kept, single replicas, Prometheus off, and a resource request. There are no feature gates, no `extraArgs` and no `config:` block.
- Only the `CA` and `SelfSigned` issuers are used: `selfsigned-bootstrap` and `mesh-ca`. There are no ACME, Vault, Venafi or DNS01 resources. A grep for ingress, ACME and CertificateRequest across `env/` found nothing.
- The chain is `selfsigned-bootstrap` -> `mesh-root-ca` (Certificate, `isCA`, ECDSA-256) -> `mesh-ca` ClusterIssuer -> `ledger-tls` and `checkout-tls`. Both leaf certificates are ECDSA-256 with a 720h duration and 240h `renewBefore`.
- Consumers:
  - `ledger` is nginx. It mounts the Secret `ledger-tls` at `/tls`, uses `ssl_client_certificate /tls/ca.crt` with `ssl_verify_client on`, and the config is read at start-up.
  - `checkout` is a curl loop. It re-reads `/tls/*` on every call and verifies ledger against `ca.crt` from its own Secret.
- Argo CD syncs automatically with `prune: true`, `selfHeal: true` and `ServerSideApply=true`. cert-manager is in wave 0, pki in wave 1, payments in wave 2.

## Affected

### 1. `rotationPolicy` default changes from `Never` to `Always` (breaking, on by default)

This is the one that matters most.
Evidence: upgrade guide item 1, release notes lines 109-148, and the CRD description change in `rendered/manifest.diff` ("Default is `Always`").

- **`ledger-tls` and `checkout-tls`: affected.** Neither sets `privateKey.rotationPolicy`, so from 1.18 each renewal generates a new key. Before, the key stayed the same across renewals.
  - Renewal happens roughly every 20 days (720h - 240h). The first renewal after the upgrade is the first rotation.
  - No re-issuance is forced at upgrade time. Rotation applies only when a re-issuance happens.
  - Why it matters here: nginx loads `tls.crt` and `tls.key` once, at start or reload. Nothing in the repo reloads it when the Secret changes.
    - This problem already exists today. A renewed certificate also does not reach a running nginx, so ledger's served certificate would expire after 30 days.
    - Key rotation adds a second risk. Kubernetes swaps the Secret volume atomically, but nginx opens the two files separately. A reload or worker start that straddles a swap can read a new `tls.crt` with an old `tls.key`, or the reverse. With a constant key that race was harmless. With a rotating key it produces a cert/key mismatch error.
    - `checkout` re-reads the files on every curl invocation, so it has the same small race.
  - Conclusion: this is a latent hazard, not an immediate failure. Verify the reload story for ledger (see the tests below).
- **`mesh-root-ca`: not affected, and the reason is an explicit setting.**
  - `env/platform/pki/overlays/prod/mesh-root-ca-prod.yaml` sets `rotationPolicy: Never`, and `clusters/prod/pki.yaml` deploys the `prod` overlay.
  - This setting is critical. If the root's key were rotated at its next renewal (1 year, 720h before expiry), the new root would sign new leaves, but every leaf's `ca.crt` in the Secrets is a snapshot of the old root.
  - Ledger and checkout trust only what is in `ca.crt`, and nothing here distributes the new root to both sides atomically. Mutual TLS would break until both Secrets and both workloads were refreshed. That would be an outage of the payments mesh.
  - Caveat: I could only read the Kustomize inputs. `rendered/` contains only the Helm output, so I did not see a built manifest for the pki overlay. Strategic-merge patches normally merge `privateKey` and keep `algorithm` and `size`, but this must be confirmed with `kustomize build platform/pki/overlays/prod`.

### 2. `revisionHistoryLimit` default changes from nil to 1 (potentially breaking)

Evidence: upgrade guide item 2 and release notes lines 151-160.

- No Certificate in the repo sets it, so on upgrade every Certificate (all four) has its older CertificateRequests garbage collected. Only the latest is kept.
- Nothing in the repo reads CertificateRequests. I found no approver, audit exporter or policy engine.
- **Unverified:** the repo cannot show whether anything outside it (an audit pipeline, a compliance process, or incident-forensics practice) depends on historical CertificateRequests. For a payments platform this is worth asking about. The deletion is irreversible, so export first if the history has value.

### 3. Rendered chart changes with a rollout footprint (not in the release-notes breaking list)

Evidence: `rendered/manifest.diff`.

- The ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding `cert-manager-controller-challenges` are removed and replaced by `cert-manager-dns01-controller-challenges` and `cert-manager-http01-controller-challenges`.
  - With Argo `prune: true`, there is a short window during rollout in which old and new bindings differ. This only affects ACME challenges, which are unused here, so there is no functional impact.
  - It does matter for anyone who has bound to or audited the old role name. Search for external references.
- The webhook liveness and readiness probes change from `port: 6080` to the named port `healthcheck`. The container does define `name: healthcheck` on 6080 (`rendered/to.yaml:12355-12356`), so this is consistent. I verified it in the render.
- New CRD content: `signatureAlgorithm`, `profile`, Vault `serverName`, and the `iss` and `ciss` shortNames. These are additive.
  - **Check `iss` and `ciss` against other CRDs and any scripts or aliases on the cluster.**
- CRDs are installed via the chart (`crds.enabled`, `keep: true`). Because of that, the CRD update will ride on this Argo sync. `ServerSideApply=true` is set, which avoids the annotation-size limit on the large CRDs.
- The webhook is a validating and mutating webhook for every cert-manager resource. Argo ordering matters: pki (wave 1) must not apply while the new webhook is not yet ready.

## Not affected

| Item | Why |
|---|---|
| HTTP01 `PathType: Exact` and the ingress-nginx incompatibility | There are no ACME issuers and no Ingress resources in `env/`. |
| ACME profiles, Vault `serverName`, Venafi URL, Cloudflare and Route53 fixes | No ACME, Vault or Venafi issuers are configured. |
| `ValidateCAA` gate removal | The gate is not set in `values.yaml`. |
| `AdditionalCertificateOutputFormats` and `UseDomainQualifiedFinalizer` promoted to GA | No gate overrides, and no `additionalOutputFormats` on any Certificate. |
| OperatorHub discontinuation | Installed via the Helm chart, not OLM. |
| ServiceMonitor and metrics port changes | `prometheus.enabled: false`. Note this also means there are no cert-expiry alerts to benefit from the new `not_after` metrics. |
| `--extra-certificate-annotations` | New and opt-in. No Ingress or Gateway resources exist. |
| Kubernetes 1.31 | The chart's `kubeVersion` is `>= 1.22.0-0` in both versions. |
| `global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole` | This value is in the chart's `values.yaml` for 1.18.0 but was reverted in 1.18.2 per the release notes. It is unset here and unimportant. |

## Version choice: v1.18.0 specifically

- Targeting the first patch of a minor is unnecessary risk. The release notes list 1.18.1 to 1.18.6. 1.18.1 adds the `ACMEHTTP01IngressPathTypeExact` gate and 1.18.2 reverts a Helm option. 1.18.3 fixes an unexpected re-issuance on `issuerRef` kind/group defaulting. 1.18.5 fixes a DoS panic and a re-issuance loop. 1.18.6 patches `CVE-2025-68121`.
  - Even though this environment's issuerRefs are explicit (group and kind set on every Certificate), prefer the latest 1.18.x over 1.18.0. I recommend a retarget to 1.18.6 as the minimum.
- Security advisory `GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258` (the copy in `upstream/` is an HTML capture of the advisory page): "Direct ACME Challenge resources can bypass Issuer DNS01 solver policy". It is rated high.
  - It affects `>= 1.18.0, <= 1.20.2`, with fixes only in 1.19.6 and 1.20.3. There is no 1.18.x fix, so upgrading to any 1.18 puts the cluster inside the affected range, where 1.17.2 is outside it.
  - Exploitability here is **very low**. It needs a ClusterIssuer with a DNS01 solver, and there are none. There is only a CA issuer and a SelfSigned issuer. It is, however, a reason to treat 1.18 as a stepping stone to 1.19.6+ rather than a resting place.
  - I read the advisory's metadata and summary only. I did not verify the versions beyond what it states.
- Is 1.17.2 itself still supported? That is not answered by the provided material (`upstream/.../releases/README.md` was not read). Check it, since it bears on how urgent this upgrade is.

## Evidence limits and missing information

1. No built Kustomize output. I could not confirm the rendered `mesh-root-ca` has `rotationPolicy: Never`. I also could not confirm the leaf Certificates render as expected.
2. No live cluster state. Unknown: the current Certificate and Secret status, the notAfter dates and renewal timing for each certificate (which determines when the first key rotation will happen), the actual number of CertificateRequests, and whether anything in the cluster watches them.
3. The nginx reload behaviour of `ledger` is not visible. There is no reloader sidecar, no Reloader/stakater annotation, and no `shareProcessNamespace`. Deployments mount the Secret as a volume with no checksum annotation.
4. Mesh trust distribution: `ca.crt` is copied into leaf Secrets at issuance. The repo shows no mechanism for pushing a changed root to workloads, so any future root change is a manual, coordinated event. This is out of scope for 1.18 but is the reason point 1 matters.
5. Cluster-wide cert-manager consumers outside this repo. ORIENTATION.md says the repo is complete, but other teams' Certificates, `cert-manager.io/*` annotations on other resources, and external tools (cmctl, approver-policy, trust-manager, csi-driver) are not visible. Any Certificate elsewhere lacking an explicit `rotationPolicy` or `revisionHistoryLimit` gets the new defaults.
6. Argo CD application health under the pruned and replaced RBAC objects, and the webhook-readiness ordering, were not testable from files alone.

## Tests and checks before proceeding

1. `kustomize build env/platform/pki/overlays/prod` and `.../apps/payments/overlays/prod`. Confirm that `mesh-root-ca` has `privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never` with `algorithm: ECDSA` and `size: 256` preserved. Confirm the leaf Certificates have no rotationPolicy.
2. `kubectl get certificate,certificaterequest -A -o wide` on prod. Record all Certificates and their renewal times. List the CertificateRequests that will be deleted, and export them if there is any audit need.
3. **Decide the leaf-key policy explicitly rather than inheriting a default.** Either set `rotationPolicy: Always` on `ledger-tls` and `checkout-tls` on purpose, or set `Never` to keep today's behaviour. Doing this in a commit *before* the upgrade makes the behaviour change independent of the version change. Set `revisionHistoryLimit` explicitly too if history is wanted. Do not rely on the gate `DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false`, because 1.19 removes it.
4. In staging (a cluster with the same issuer chain), upgrade and then force a renewal: `cmctl renew -n payments ledger-tls checkout-tls`. Verify that:
   - the `tls.key` changes;
   - checkout still reaches ledger (`ledger ok: client=...`);
   - ledger actually serves the new certificate (`openssl s_client`), which shows whether nginx picks up changed files or needs a reload;
   - nothing logs a key/cert mismatch.
   If ledger needs a reload, add a reload mechanism (a reloader controller, a sidecar, or a checksum rollout) before the first production renewal after the upgrade.

# cert-manager v1.17.2 -> v1.18.0: impact assessment for the prod payments cluster

## Verdict

**No documented breaking change is a hard blocker for this environment, but the upgrade is not a no-op. One breaking change (the `rotationPolicy` default flip) changes runtime behaviour for two live Certificates, and one (the `revisionHistoryLimit` default) deletes data on first reconcile.**
The upgrade is acceptable to proceed with, subject to the pre-flight checks at the end. The most important check is one I could not perform from this repository: confirming that the rendered `mesh-root-ca` carries `rotationPolicy: Never` and that the live nginx and curl workloads cope with key rotation.

## What this environment actually uses

- cert-manager is installed from the Helm chart with minimal values (`env/platform/cert-manager/values.yaml`): CRDs enabled and kept, single replicas, Prometheus off, and a resource request. There are no feature gates, no `extraArgs` and no `config:` block.
- Only the `CA` and `SelfSigned` issuers are used: `selfsigned-bootstrap` and `mesh-ca`. There are no ACME, Vault, Venafi or DNS01 resources. A grep for ingress, ACME and CertificateRequest across `env/` found nothing.
- The chain is `selfsigned-bootstrap` -> `mesh-root-ca` (Certificate, `isCA`, ECDSA-256) -> `mesh-ca` ClusterIssuer -> `ledger-tls` and `checkout-tls`. Both leaf certificates are ECDSA-256 with a 720h duration and 240h `renewBefore`.
- Consumers:
  - `ledger` is nginx. It mounts the Secret `ledger-tls` at `/tls`, uses `ssl_client_certificate /tls/ca.crt` with `ssl_verify_client on`, and the config is read at start-up.
  - `checkout` is a curl loop. It re-reads `/tls/*` on every call and verifies ledger against `ca.crt` from its own Secret.
- Argo CD syncs automatically with `prune: true`, `selfHeal: true` and `ServerSideApply=true`. cert-manager is in wave 0, pki in wave 1, payments in wave 2.

## Affected

### 1. `rotationPolicy` default changes from `Never` to `Always` (breaking, on by default)

This is the one that matters most.
Evidence: upgrade guide item 1, release notes lines 109-148, and the CRD description change in `rendered/manifest.diff` ("Default is `Always`").

- **`ledger-tls` and `checkout-tls`: affected.** Neither sets `privateKey.rotationPolicy`, so from 1.18 each renewal generates a new key. Before, the key stayed the same across renewals.
  - Renewal happens roughly every 20 days (720h - 240h). The first renewal after the upgrade is the first rotation.
  - No re-issuance is forced at upgrade time. Rotation applies only when a re-issuance happens.
  - Why it matters here: nginx loads `tls.crt` and `tls.key` once, at start or reload. Nothing in the repo reloads it when the Secret changes.
    - This problem already exists today. A renewed certificate also does not reach a running nginx, so ledger's served certificate would expire after 30 days.
    - Key rotation adds a second risk. Kubernetes swaps the Secret volume atomically, but nginx opens the two files separately. A reload or worker start that straddles a swap can read a new `tls.crt` with an old `tls.key`, or the reverse. With a constant key that race was harmless. With a rotating key it produces a cert/key mismatch error.
    - `checkout` re-reads the files on every curl invocation, so it has the same small race.
  - Conclusion: this is a latent hazard, not an immediate failure. Verify the reload story for ledger (see the tests below).
- **`mesh-root-ca`: not affected, and the reason is an explicit setting.**
  - `env/platform/pki/overlays/prod/mesh-root-ca-prod.yaml` sets `rotationPolicy: Never`, and `clusters/prod/pki.yaml` deploys the `prod` overlay.
  - This setting is critical. If the root's key were rotated at its next renewal (1 year, 720h before expiry), the new root would sign new leaves, but every leaf's `ca.crt` in the Secrets is a snapshot of the old root.
  - Ledger and checkout trust only what is in `ca.crt`, and nothing here distributes the new root to both sides atomically. Mutual TLS would break until both Secrets and both workloads were refreshed. That would be an outage of the payments mesh.
  - Caveat: I could only read the Kustomize inputs. `rendered/` contains only the Helm output, so I did not see a built manifest for the pki overlay. Strategic-merge patches normally merge `privateKey` and keep `algorithm` and `size`, but this must be confirmed with `kustomize build platform/pki/overlays/prod`.

### 2. `revisionHistoryLimit` default changes from nil to 1 (potentially breaking)

Evidence: upgrade guide item 2 and release notes lines 151-160.

- No Certificate in the repo sets it, so on upgrade every Certificate (all four) has its older CertificateRequests garbage collected. Only the latest is kept.
- Nothing in the repo reads CertificateRequests. I found no approver, audit exporter or policy engine.
- **Unverified:** the repo cannot show whether anything outside it (an audit pipeline, a compliance process, or incident-forensics practice) depends on historical CertificateRequests.   - With Argo `prune: true`, there is a short window during rollout in which old and new bindings differ. This only affects ACME challenges, which are unused here, so there is no functional impact.
  - It does matter for anyone who has bound to or audited the old role name. Search for external references.
- The webhook liveness and readiness probes change from `port: 6080` to the named port `healthcheck`. The container does define `name: healthcheck` on 6080 (`rendered/to.yaml:12355-12356`), so this is consistent. I verified it in the render.

  - **Check `iss` and `ciss` against other CRDs and any scripts or aliases on the cluster.**

I've written the assessment to `scratch/assessment.md`. Nothing in the 1.18.0 release blocks this upgrade, but two of its default changes do affect this environment.

I didn't check whether the 1.17 line is still supported, because I didn't read the releases README. That affects how urgent the upgrade is.

**What is affected**
- **Private key rotation:** `ledger-tls` and `checkout-tls` don't set `rotationPolicy`, so they will get a new private key at each renewal, roughly every 20 days. The first rotation happens at the first renewal after the upgrade.
  - The `ledger` nginx only loads its certificate and key at start or reload, and nothing in the repo reloads it when the Secret changes. Rotating keys adds a risk that a reload picks up a new certificate with an old key.
  - I can't tell from the repo whether the live `ledger` pods cope with this. A forced renewal in staging would show it.
- **Root CA:** `mesh-root-ca` is protected only by the explicit `rotationPolicy: Never` in the prod overlay. If its key rotated, the mutual TLS between services would break, because every service's CA certificate would still point at the old root. I couldn't confirm the overlay renders that setting, because `rendered/` only has the Helm output. Run `kustomize build` on the prod overlay to check.
- **Certificate request history:** older CertificateRequests are deleted on upgrade, because the default `revisionHistoryLimit` changes from unlimited to 1. Nothing in the repo reads them. I can't see whether anything outside it, such as audit or forensics processes, depends on them.
- **Rendered diff:** the `cert-manager-controller-challenges` role is replaced by two new roles, which Argo CD will prune and recreate. This only matters for ACME challenges, which you don't use.
  - The webhook probes switch to a named port that does exist in the render.
  - The new `iss` and `ciss` short names should be checked for clashes with other tools or aliases.

**What is not affected**
- The ingress-nginx `Exact` path change, ACME profiles and the Vault and Venafi changes don't apply. There are no ACME, Vault, Venafi or Ingress resources, only the self-signed bootstrap issuer and the CA issuer.
- No cert-manager feature gates are set, Prometheus is off, and Kubernetes 1.31 is within the chart's range.

**Version choice**
- I'd target the latest 1.18.x (1.18.6) rather than 1.18.0, since the later patch releases fix a re-issuance loop and a denial-of-service panic.
- The security advisory in `upstream/` (rated high) affects 1.18.0 through 1.20.2. It is fixed only in 1.19.6 and 1.20.3, so any 1.18 release is inside the affected range. It isn't exploitable here because there is no DNS01 issuer, but 1.18 should be a stop on the way to 1.19.6 or later.

Before upgrading, set `rotationPolicy` and `revisionHistoryLimit` explicitly on the leaf certificates so the behaviour doesn't depend on a default. The full list of pre-flight tests is in the assessment.
